A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEMENTO research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix A report original TSP and CVRP experiments, including memory-based adaptation, zero-shot combination with COMPASS, and evaluation on size-500 instances.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds runtime scaling measurements, memory-feature ablations, and training-validation curves.

M1.justification: The memory retrieval, MLP-based additive logit correction, budgeted training objective, and COMPASS combination procedure are retained. V2 provides a fuller feature list and explicit inference description, without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: The TSP/CVRP solution-quality benchmarks at sizes 100, 125, 150, 200, and 500 remain. The new runtime analysis additionally evaluates CVRP instances up to size 1,000 (Appendix A.4), extending instance-size coverage for computational measurements.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 3 and Table 2 add SGBS comparisons for TSP/CVRP and HGS comparisons for CVRP, materially broadening the benchmark to additional tree-search and classical-solver comparators. SGBS scores are imported from Choo et al. rather than newly run. EAS-Emb identifies the retained EAS baseline; FER and MARCO are discussed but not benchmarked.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled timing sweeps over instance size and decoder depth, plus feature-subset controls. Appendix A.4 specifies separate starting-point and sequential-attempt budgets for the timing sweeps. Appendix A.1 also changes standard-benchmark timing from v1's total-time description to per-instance reporting. Original accuracy-evaluation budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds return/log-probability-only versus full-feature comparisons and cumulative feature ablations (Figures 8–9). Figure 7 adds runtime sensitivity to instance size and decoder depth, while Appendix H adds training-progress diagnostics. These substantially expand analysis beyond v1's retained update-rule heatmaps and search-budget comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the standard-deviation visualization for the COMPASS combination experiment. Neither reports new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures; the added curves do not introduce such reporting.

E6.justification: Original solution-quality results are retained, but v2 adds SGBS/HGS scores and runtime, ablation, and training curves. For example, the new HGS row reports CVRP100 tour length 15.563. Timing entries also change: TSP100 POMO greedy is reported as 16 seconds in v1 Table 3 and 0.16 seconds in v2 Table 2, alongside the revised timing basis.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, optimization objectives, and REINFORCE derivative argument are retained. Appendix F relocates the argument from v1 Section 3.2; Appendix B explicitly writes out the already-described rectified-improvement loss and logarithmic weighting. These do not introduce a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The central memory-adaptation, zero-shot transfer, and 11-of-12 state-of-the-art claims remain. V2's abstract and conclusion additionally claim superiority over tree search and favorable runtime scaling with instance and base-solver size, extending the asserted benefits.

C2.justification: V2 drops v1's explanation that larger logit-update amplitude explains data efficiency and emphasizes additional contextual inputs and budget-dependent exploration. It adds SGBS comparability qualifications and explanations of COMPASS timing differences. The limitations also suggest replacing the MLP with an extracted mathematical update to reduce overhead.

D1.justification: V2 documents additional stored features, the explicit weighted loss, and fixed-parameter inference. Appendix A.3 discloses COMPASS's latent-vector/starting-point allocation and clarifies the CVRP500 dataset source. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware information, and code/checkpoint access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds FER, MARCO, and HGS references and contrasts embedding or graph-based adaptation with MEMENTO's direct logit updates. It also explains the exclusion of supervised LEHD comparisons and removes the Williams reference. SGBS's underlying work was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain. V2 reorganizes the method explanation into clearer storage, retrieval, processing, and inference passages, refines related-work headings and abstract/conclusion wording, and expands appendix explanations.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1 and adds a memory-processing diagram. It replaces the separate benchmark bar charts with a table/chart composite, combines v1's large-instance table with new timing plots, and adds Figures 8–10. Budget heatmaps gain explanatory labels, and table placement and document layout are substantially revised.

improvement.justification: The feature ablations, runtime scaling tests, and fuller method documentation make MEMENTO's mechanism and practical efficiency more assessable than in v1. The gains are tempered by unmatched SGBS settings and broad superiority wording: v2 Table 2 reports a lower TSP200 gap for SGBS than MEMENTO, 0.619% versus 0.664%. Overall, evidence and clarity improve, while the core accuracy results remain unchanged.
